title: RBAC v2: enforce permissions on API key management endpoints
author: Benji Okafor
body:
Title: RBAC v2: enforce permissions on API key management endpoints

Context
We’re migrating control-plane authorization from RBAC v1 (feature-gated, coarse checks) to RBAC v2 (resource/action/scope). API key management is one of the highest leverage surfaces for privilege escalation and needs least-privilege enforcement before we can move more endpoints into enforcement mode.

This PR wires RBAC v2 permission checks into the API key endpoints:
- POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/keys (create)
- POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/keys/{key_id}:rotate (rotate)
- DELETE /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/keys/{key_id} (revoke)
- GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects/{project_id}/keys (list)

Also adds a test matrix to ensure least-privilege behavior and verifies we return standardized 403 responses with reason codes.

What changed
- Added RBAC v2 checks in the api-keys handler layer (service-side) using the shared authz middleware.
- Introduced explicit RBAC v2 actions for key operations.
- Ensured scope is project-scoped (org+project) and actor is read from request auth context.
- Added integration tests covering allow/deny for default roles (Org Admin, Developer, Read-only, Billing Admin).
- Added audit log enrichment hook points (no schema changes here; just ensured the authz decision context is populated for the audit logging layer).

RBAC v2 actions (new)
- controlplane.apikey.create
- controlplane.apikey.rotate
- controlplane.apikey.revoke
- controlplane.apikey.list

Evaluation semantics
- Deny-by-default.
- Use the same decision path as other RBAC v2 enforced endpoints (policy cache + evaluator).
- In shadow mode we still record RBAC v2 decisions, but these endpoints are now “enforce when enabled” behind the existing RBAC_V2_ENFORCE_KEYS flag.

Error handling
- Unauthorized access returns HTTP 403 with standardized error payload:
  - code: AUTHZ_DENIED
  - reason: one of AUTHZ_MISSING_PERMISSION | AUTHZ_SCOPE_MISMATCH | AUTHZ_POLICY_NOT_LOADED
  - message: stable customer-facing message (no permission names leaked unless debug header is present)

Tests added
- api_keys_rbac_test.go: table-driven integration tests against the control-plane router
  - verifies correct allow/deny for each operation by role
  - ensures list returns redacted/limited fields for roles that can list but not manage (where applicable)
  - ensures rotate/revoke can’t be performed across projects
- Added negative coverage for legacy RBAC v1-only tokens while RBAC v2 is in dual mode (ensures behavior remains unchanged when flag is off)

Example snippet (handler)
Before:
- API key endpoints validated project membership but did not require explicit permission beyond coarse “project admin” checks in some call paths.

After:
- Each handler declares a v2 action and calls Authorize(ctx, actor, action, scope).

Pseudo-code:
- action := authz.Action("controlplane.apikey.rotate")
- scope := authz.Scope{OrgID: orgID, ProjectID: projectID}
- if err := authz.Authorize(ctx, actor, action, scope); err != nil { return authz.ToHTTP(err) }

Files/areas touched (high level)
- control-plane/service/api_keys/*
- control-plane/authz/actions.go
- control-plane/http/errors/authz.go
- control-plane/service/api_keys/api_keys_rbac_test.go
- control-plane/testutil/roles/*

Commits
1) authz: define apikey actions and wire handler checks
2) api-keys: enforce create/rotate/revoke/list permissions + scope validation
3) tests: add role matrix + cross-project negative coverage
4) polish: standardize 403 reason codes + log fields

Rollout notes
- This is safe to land prior to global enforcement since it’s guarded by RBAC_V2_ENFORCE_KEYS.
- Metrics emitted:
  - authz_eval_latency_ms{action=controlplane.apikey.*}
  - authz_denied_total{reason=...}
  - authz_shadow_denied_total{action=...}

Checklist
- [x] RBAC v2 actions are named per conventions
- [x] Enforced check is in service (not only gateway)
- [x] 403 errors use standardized schema
- [x] Tests cover least privilege + scope mismatch
- [x] Added structured logs for allow/deny decisions

Links
- Linear: ENG-5385 (Integrate RBAC v2 checks into control-plane endpoints)
- Umbrella: ENG-5381 (RBAC v2 + permission inventory)

Review conversation (highlights)

Kaitlyn Nguyen (Authz implementation lead):
“Thanks for the table-driven tests. Can we make sure Billing Admin is denied for create/rotate/revoke but allowed for list only if we explicitly want that? For least privilege, I think Billing Admin should be denied for all key actions including list.”

Benji Okafor (author):
“Good call. I updated the matrix: Billing Admin is now denied for list as well. Only Org Admin + Developer can list keys; Read-only is denied. (We can revisit if PM wants a ‘Security auditor’ role that can list but not rotate.)”

Marcus Lin (Security exec owner):
“Make sure we don’t leak key_id existence to unauthorized actors. Revoke/rotate should return 403 before 404 if the actor lacks permission.”

Benji Okafor:
“Updated ordering so authz check happens before key lookup. Tests added to ensure we return 403 for unauthorized regardless of key existence.”

Brian Murphy (API surface reviewer):
“Any backwards compatibility risk with clients relying on list returning keys for read-only roles?”

Benji Okafor:
“Read-only never had a documented guarantee here; also still behind RBAC_V2_ENFORCE_KEYS. When the flag is off, behavior remains unchanged. When on, we’ll include this in release notes / comms.”

Amara Diallo (API gateway integration):
“Do we also have gateway enforcement? I’m fine with service-side checks as source of truth but want to ensure we don’t double-check in a way that diverges.”

Benji Okafor:
“Service-side is canonical. Gateway stays in ‘pass-through’ mode for now; it only attaches actor context and request IDs. No divergent policy logic.”

CI
- build (linux/amd64): pass
- unit tests: pass
- integration tests: pass
- lint/staticcheck: pass

Outcome
Merged via squash.

Release note (internal)
When RBAC_V2_ENFORCE_KEYS is enabled, API key create/rotate/revoke/list require explicit RBAC v2 permissions (project-scoped). Unauthorized calls return standardized 403 with reason codes and are captured in authz decision logs.
